title: a ticket whose build is on main has crossed BUILDME
intention: build_inspector reds every ticket whose cursor stands at a stage before BUILDME in its own workflow path (THINKME, TICKETME, FIXME, any stage the path places ahead of BUILDME) while the cairn repo's main carries a commit whose subject names its id before the subject's first colon, that changes a build path (outside press_office/, proofs/ and validations/, not *.md, not a component's history.json or state.json, not .artifact-journal.jsonl), and that is newer than the ticket's latest forward BUILDME crossing (or the ticket never crossed BUILDME). The red names the ticket, its cursor and the commits. A ticket at or past BUILDME, one named only after the colon, one whose only naming commits are doc commits or its red-first proof (proof, seal, journals), or one whose naming code commits all predate its latest forward BUILDME crossing, is not red.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendell by census over commons main and origin/main (5399 commits): 113 tickets read [TICKETME:...]; 47 of them are named by at least one origin/main commit; 31 of the 47 carry a 'Linux seal of its proofs' or reseal commit, and 32 of the 47 have no fixme at all, so they were built, landed and sealed without a chart attempt or a BUILDME crossing. Two of two tickets the orchestrator picked as unbuilt (404d3f6f3d9b, 3ba20f30a585) were already built and sealed on main. The land and seal path is the integrator's own scripts (the orchestrator grepped the cairn repo: no python component moves a cursor there), so the rule cannot live there; it is a rule that matters (Law 4) and today is policy. A sieve reading the two records (commons state, repo log) makes the disagreement a red instead of a thing a mind finds by accident.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy), Law 5 (a thing and its story may not contradict: the repo says built, the state says TICKETME), Law 9 (red is the default; a built ticket whose cursor says otherwise is a visible red, not a lost one).
how: A repo-level scan in inspector.py, called by inspect() beside slate_reach and unbuilt_intentions (not a per-component row sieve): read every tickets/*.state.json in the sibling CairnCommons for a [TICKETME:...] cursor (via _workflow_cursor), run one `git log --format=%H%x09%s --name-only` over the cairn repo's main, index commits whose subject names a ticket id (twelve lowercase hex), keep those that change at least one path outside press_office/ and outside *.md, and emit one finding per ticket id with its commit shas. RULE 1: the sieve reads records only and imports no machine. Proof: a scratch cairn repo and scratch commons, red first.

measured.saw: 113 tickets at [TICKETME:...] on commons main; 47 named by an origin/main commit subject; 31 of those 47 with a seal or reseal commit; 32 of the 47 with no fixme; 13 with a chart/orient-shaped last fixme, 2 with another gate's. The orchestrator found no python component in the cairn repo that moves a cursor on land (the land and seal path is the integrator's scripts). 217c82fe7b57 (a ticket built before hex ids names its build commits for the hollow) is adjacent, not a sibling: it anchors the hollow's build commits, it does not red a built-but-uncrossed ticket.
measured.how: census script over CairnCommons/tickets/*.state.json and `git log origin/main` (scratchpad census_tm.py), the orchestrator's grep of the cairn repo, and reading ticket 217c82fe7b57's intention

measured.saw: False-positive census on origin/main (git log --name-only) against 114 [TICKETME:...] tickets: 43 are named by a code commit (the 47 upper bound drops 4 doc-only: 4c4a, 12443, dd79, d421, so the built count is at most 43, not 47); 42 of the 43 have a code commit whose subject names the id BEFORE the first colon, 1 (aa05710a5124) only after it, a passing mention; 8 of the 43 carry only seal commits in that lead position and 34 carry at least one non-seal lead commit (a build or red-first proof). So the measured built count is 42, and the lead-colon rule removes the one false positive.

Its last forward BUILDME before that was 489b5b2fa on 2026-11-13. A TICKETME-only cursor test misses this ticket.

outcomes.claim: a ticket whose cursor stands before BUILDME in its path (TICKETME or FIXME) and whose id is named by a code commit newer than its latest forward BUILDME crossing is reported, with that commit's sha and the cursor
outcomes.via: the scan lives in build_inspector's inspector.py beside slate_reach and is wired into inspect(); the git read is one `git log` over main, never one per ticket. D-widen (orchestrator, 2026-11-22): the cursor test is every stage before BUILDME in the ticket's own path, not TICKETME alone, because the rule broke at FIXME (88e30cde9bd4, measured). 'Before BUILDME' is read from the workflow string's path order through workflow_grammar, never a hand list of stage names; 'newer than' compares the commit's committer time with the latest forward BUILDME crossing's at from cairn.tools.base.crossings. one proof over a scratch git repo and commons, one tooth per clause, red first.

outcomes.claim: a ticket whose only naming commit changes press_office/ or a .md file, a ticket named only after the subject's first colon, a ticket at or past BUILDME with a code commit, and a TICKETME ticket named by no commit are each NOT reported, and a FIXME ticket whose naming code commits all predate its latest forward BUILDME crossing is NOT reported, and a TICKETME ticket whose only naming commit is its red-first proof (proofs/, validations/, history.json, state.json, .artifact-journal.jsonl) is NOT reported
outcomes.via: a build path is any changed path outside press_office/, proofs/ and validations/, not named history.json, state.json or .artifact-journal.jsonl, and not *.md; a commit names a ticket only when the id stands before the subject's first colon (the integrator's 'id: what' and 'id, id: what' forms). The reported tickets are the integrator's re-chart backlog, not tickets of their own.
